claims.claim_summary: Structures solution ideas as hierarchical levels ranging from high-level strategies to detailed plans.

evidence_spans.source_text: With X and Y as in Section 3, we fix a depth n ∈ Z≥0, and introduce hierarchy sets Z0, . . . , Zn. An element z = (z0, . . . , zn) ∈ Z := Z0 × · · · × Zn will be called a hierarchy. In practice, a hierarchy z ∈ Z for a problem x ∈ X is intended to represent a semantically meaningful idea, plan, or approach for constructing a solution y ∈ Y for x at different levels of granularity: From a detailed solution sketch z0 to a coarse description of the overarching idea zn.
The concrete prompt templates in Appendix A.3 use two levels (n = 1): a detailed plan z0 and a coarse proof idea z1; neither is required to consist of executable Lean commands.

claims.claim_summary: Distinguishes the method from prior work by repeatedly retraining the same backbone retrospectively.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: This differs from the forward generation of thoughts and tactics in Lean-STaR’s expert iterations, and from DeepInsight’s retrospective rationale generation using a teacher model: our loop repeatedly performs retrospective hierarchy generation with the same backbone that learns to predict and use the resulting hierarchies.

evidence_spans.source_text: The system, parametrized by a collection of parameters θ, consists of three components. While these components may have component-specific parameters, they share a backbone network which accounts for the majority of parameters

The centerpiece of our method is an alternating training loop. In each iteration, the current hindsight component reconstructs ideas for a batch of problems with supplied solutions. We then jointly train all three components using the resulting data together with previously collected examples.

This differs from the forward generation of thoughts and tactics in Lean-STaR’s expert iterations, and from DeepInsight’s retrospective rationale generation using a teacher model: our loop repeatedly performs retrospective hierarchy generation with the same backbone that learns to predict and use the resulting hierarchies.
